The NWS active alerts feed for Arizona, checked directly today, shows no Excessive Heat Warning, Heat Advisory, or Red Flag Warning active anywhere in the state (Source: National Weather Service). No flood watch is in effect for the Tucson area today. Hike before 7am or after 7pm and carry extra water.

tumamoc-hill.note: No current 2026 closure notice could be found for Tumamoc Hill today; standard public walking hours remain 4am to 10pm daily, and visitors must stay on the paved road (Source: University of Arizona, not freshly reconfirmed against a live page today). The NWS active alerts feed for Arizona, checked directly today, shows no Excessive Heat Warning, Heat Advisory, or Red Flag Warning active anywhere in the state (Source: National Weather Service). No flood watch is in effect for the Tucson area today. This trail follows a paved road with no creek or wash crossings. Carry extra water.

wasson-peak.note: The National Park Service confirmed containment of the Box Fire in Saguaro National Park reached 100% in June 2026 and all park trails and campgrounds, including Wasson Peak Trail, reopened at that time; Saguaro National Park's projects-and-closures page, rechecked directly today, lists only an unrelated Signal Hill Picnic Area and access road closure in the Tucson Mountain District (West), with alternate access to that area via the Cactus Wren or Manville trails (Source: National Park Service). A portion of Golden Gate Road between Sendero Esperanza Trailhead and Picture Rocks Road remains permanently converted to a multi-use trail and closed to vehicles, unrelated to this trail. The NWS active alerts feed for Arizona, checked directly today, shows no Excessive Heat Warning, Heat Advisory, or Red Flag Warning active anywhere in the state (Source: National Weather Service). No flood watch is in effect for the Tucson area today. Hike before 7am or after 7pm and carry extra water.

valley-view-overlook.note: Saguaro National Park's projects-and-closures page, rechecked directly today, lists only the unrelated Signal Hill Picnic Area and access road closure in the Tucson Mountain District (West); the Box Fire that affected parts of the park earlier this year reached 100% containment in June 2026 with all trails since reopened (Source: National Park Service). The only other standing change near this area is the permanent conversion of a Golden Gate Road segment to a multi-use trail between Sendero Esperanza Trailhead and Picture Rocks Road, unrelated to this trail. The NWS active alerts feed for Arizona, checked directly today, shows no Excessive Heat Warning, Heat Advisory, or Red Flag Warning active anywhere in the state (Source: National Weather Service). No flood watch is in effect for the Tucson area today. Hike before 7am or after 7pm and carry extra water.

tanque-verde-ridge.note: Saguaro National Park's projects-and-closures page, rechecked directly today, lists no closures in the Rincon Mountain District (East), and no alert names Tanque Verde Ridge Trail; the Box Fire that affected the park earlier this year reached 100% containment in June 2026 (Source: National Park Service). Call the Rincon Mountain Visitor Center at 520-733-5153 for specifics on current trail conditions, including stump holes, slick surfaces, fire-weakened trees, and flash flood risk in older burn scars. The NWS active alerts feed for Arizona, checked directly today, shows no Excessive Heat Warning, Heat Advisory, or Red Flag Warning active anywhere in the state (Source: National Weather Service). No flood watch is in effect for the Tucson area today. Hike before 7am or after 7pm and carry extra water.

south-kaibab-ooh-aah.note: Grand Canyon National Park's Key Hiking Messages page, last updated October 27, 2026 and rechecked directly today, states South Kaibab Trail is open from the South Kaibab Trailhead to Black Bridge, which covers Ooh Aah Point and Cedar Ridge well within the open section; this follows the park's reopening, announced October 26, of the section below the Tipoff that had been closed since the late-August flooding (Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park). Black Bridge and Silver Bridge, which span the Colorado River, remain closed due to flash flood hazard, so through-hikes to Phantom Ranch or the North Rim are not possible, but South Kaibab Trail itself is open for day hikes to Ooh Aah Point and beyond. Potable water is available at the South Kaibab Trailhead tank; there is no reliable water source below the trailhead. This trail is fully sun exposed. The NWS active alerts feed for Arizona, checked directly today, shows no Excessive Heat Warning, Heat Advisory, or Red Flag Warning active anywhere in the state (Source: National Weather Service).

bright-angel-indian-garden.note: Grand Canyon National Park's Key Hiking Messages page, last updated October 27, 2026 and rechecked directly today, states Bright Angel Trail is open from the Bright Angel Trailhead to the River Resthouse, which covers Havasupai Gardens (formerly Indian Garden) well within the open section; the full River Trail connecting to South Kaibab has also reopened as of October 26 (Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park). A short segment between Mile-and-a-Half Resthouse and Havasupai Gardens remains closed to stock use only while crews repair trail damage; this does not affect hikers on foot. Beyond River Resthouse, Black Bridge and Silver Bridge themselves remain closed due to flash flood hazard, so Phantom Ranch and the river crossing remain inaccessible. Corridor water remains limited; confirm current status with the Backcountry Information Center at 928-638-7875 before descending. The NWS active alerts feed for Arizona, checked directly today, shows no Excessive Heat Warning, Heat Advisory, or Red Flag Warning active anywhere in the state (Source: National Weather Service).

rim-trail.note: The Rim Trail and rim overlooks are not named among the inner canyon corridor trail closures on Grand Canyon's Key Hiking Messages page, last updated October 27, 2026 and rechecked directly today, which limits its closures to trails below the rim (Black Bridge, Silver Bridge, and the entirety of North Kaibab Trail) (Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park). The NWS active alerts feed for Arizona, checked directly today, shows no Excessive Heat Warning, Heat Advisory, or Red Flag Warning active anywhere in the state (Source: National Weather Service). Use caution near the rim during any lightning.

north-kaibab-coconino.note: The entirety of North Kaibab Trail, from the North Kaibab Trailhead to Phantom Ranch, including Cottonwood Campground, remains closed following the flash flooding in Bright Angel Canyon on August 29, 2026 that destroyed footbridges and water pipeline infrastructure. Grand Canyon National Park's Key Hiking Messages page, last updated October 27, 2026 and rechecked directly today, reconfirms the full closure with no estimated reopening at this time (Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park). Phantom Ranch, Bright Angel Campground, and the Canteen remain fully closed as part of this closure. Corridor water remains off at the North Kaibab Trailhead, Supai Tunnel, Manzanita Day Use Area, and Cottonwood Campground. The NWS active alerts feed for Arizona, checked directly today, shows no Excessive Heat Warning, Heat Advisory, or Red Flag Warning active anywhere in the state (Source: National Weather Service).
